events.text: In the spring of your fifteenth year a pedlar nobody has seen before stops at your door, presses a small jade talisman into your hands, says "It is paid for, it was paid for a long time ago," and is gone before you can ask by whom. The jade is warm, and in your head a voice you have heard only once, at your birth, clears its throat.

choices.text: Hold the jade tight and listen

effects.log: The voice is young, and very far away, and it calls you something nobody has ever called you before: "Ancestor."

choices.text: Ask the jade who it is

effects.log: "Someone who would not exist without you," says the jade. "Please, keep me with you. There is a great deal to do."

events.text: On the night you turn fifteen a light falls out of a clear sky into the yard, and in the hollow it leaves you find a talisman of green jade, cool as river water, carved with a family crest you do not know. When you pick it up, the crest is yours.

choices.text: Put the jade on a cord around your neck

effects.log: The moment it touches your skin, something in your blocked meridians stirs for the first time in your life.

choices.text: Say aloud that you are listening

effects.log: For a moment the jade is silent. Then a voice, shaking a little: "It worked. Ancestor, it worked. Can you hear me?"

events.text: The jade talisman cracks in the night, a hair-thin line from one edge to the other. In the morning it is cold. You hold it for a long time, waiting for the voice from the far end of your bloodline, and it does not come. The house it spoke for has fallen, and the future it spoke from is gone with it.

effects.log: You keep it on its cord. It never speaks again, but now and then, on a cold night, you think it is a little warm.

choices.text: Bury it under the plum tree

effects.log: You bury it under the plum tree with a cup of wine. Whoever they were, they tried. That has to count for something.

events.text: The jade is brighter than it has ever been. "Ancestor," says the voice, "the house stands. In my time it stands, too: I can see the courtyard from my window, and the plum tree, and the children. Whatever was breaking is mended. This is the last time the jade can reach you. I want to give you one more thing."

choices.text: Ask it to finish mending your body

effects.log: The jade burns once against your chest, and every old wound you carry closes a little more. "There," says the voice. "Live long."

choices.text: Ask it what comes after you

effects.log: The voice tells you, quickly and quietly, the shape of the centuries to come. Then it laughs. "Do not tell anyone. I mean it."

choices.text: Ask it to stay, as only jade

effects.log: "I cannot stay," says the voice, "but the jade can." The light goes out of it gently. It stays warm, and lucky, on its cord.
